content:
While expanding the library on dynamical systems, I've encountered an issue with QuasiMeasurePreserving maps; I don't know the implementation well enough to understand what I am missing (or if there is something wrong with the implementation).

According to the documentation of Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.QuasiMeasurePreserving,

A map f : α → β is said to be quasi-measure-preserving (a.k.a. non-singular) w.r.t. measures μa and μb if it is measurable and μb s = 0 implies μa (f ⁻¹' s) = 0. That last condition can also be written μa.map f ≪ μb (the map of μa by f is absolutely continuous with respect to μb).

The latter condition μa.map f ≪ μb is the one which is actually implemented.

So, how do we prove that a map is quasi-measure-preserving? We introduce a set s in β with μb s = 0, and need to show that μa.map f s = 0.

If s is measurable, then μa.map f s = μa (f ⁻¹' s), and we get a very concrete target.

If s is not measurable, however, it seems that we are basically out of luck. There are few results in the library, and those that exist are in the wrong direction, i.e. if μa.map f s = 0 then μa (f ⁻¹' s) = 0 (MeasureTheory.Measure.le_map_apply).

At this point, I don't know how to proceed. A few ideas:

  • The documentation quoted above claims the equivalence of two properties, and it is not clear to me that they are actually equivalent. If they are, a lemma showing the equivalence is missing.
  • I don't know where the issue is. Is the definition of quasi-measure-preserving maps wrong? The condition: μb s = 0 implies μa (f ⁻¹' s) = 0 for all sets seems more manageable, but weaker; the restriction of the condition to measurable sets feels natural, but I don't know what it would break. If the definition is right, there is a need to write down some constructions ensuring that some lare families of maps are quasi-measure-preserving (measurable embeddings are in the library, but it's quite restrictive).

Paging @Johannes Hölzl , @Mario Carneiro , @Sébastien Gouëzel
You can use MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.mk to prove absolute continuity by using only measurable sets.
Works like a charm, thanks! I'll add some documentation in the file for quasi-measure-preserving maps.
